extracted.intended_audience: state environmental agencies, utilities and EGU owners/operators, industry stakeholders, and legal/regulatory practitioners involved in Clean Air Act section 111 rulemaking and implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Final EPA rule (NSPS and Emission Guidelines) setting standards and procedural requirements for greenhouse gas emissions from new, modified, reconstructed, and existing fossil fuel-fired electric generating units (EGUs), and instructions for State plans and compliance mechanisms. Covers BSER determinations, applicability/subcategorization, monitoring, recordkeeping, compliance flexibilities, and state submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key elements of determining a standard of performance (BSER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key Elements of Determining a Standard of Performance: (a) System of Emission Reduction; (b) “Adequately Demonstrated”; (c) Costs; (d) Non-Air Quality Health and Environmental Impact and Energy Requirements; (e) Sector or Nationwide Component of Factors in Determining the BSER; (f) “Best”; (g) Amount of Emissions Reductions; (h) Expanded Use and Development of Technology; (i) Achievability of the Degree of Emission Limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble lists these factors as the principal elements EPA uses when setting a BSER and standard of performance, and discusses statutory/contextual and case-law considerations for applying them (see section V.C in the preamble).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequately Demonstrated
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a candidate system of emission reduction is “adequately demonstrated” considering plain text, statutory context, legislative history, case law, and real-world demonstrations, including the compliance timeframe for demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates field demonstrations, commercial-scale projects, technology vendor statements, user statements, and applicability across operating conditions (e.g., variable load, startups/shutdowns). Preamble contains detailed sub-discussions (e.g., CCS demonstrations, capture technology demonstrations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of costs in BSER determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs are a required element in BSER selection — including capture costs, CO2 transport and sequestration costs, tax incentives (e.g., IRC Section 45Q), and comparison to other controls and prior rulemakings' costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA assesses whether costs render a candidate BSER reasonable/achievable and compares costs across options and to prior determinations; the RIA and TSD contain quantitative analyses and sensitivity runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-air quality health and environmental impacts and energy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of energy penalties, non-GHG emissions, water use, siting impacts for capture/transport/sequestration, and broader impacts on the energy sector when evaluating candidate BSER options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates these impacts alongside cost and performance (e.g., CCS energy penalty and water use), and includes regulatory/permit considerations (UIC, GHGRP) and possible mitigation/contingency measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of emissions reductions and promotion of technology
rubrics_metrics.description: The degree to which a candidate BSER reduces CO2 emissions and whether the standard promotes the development and implementation of emission-reducing technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA weighs demonstrated and projected CO2 reductions and how a standard might accelerate technology deployment; discussion appears across BSER rationales for CCS, hydrogen, efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Achievability of the degree of emission limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination that the degree of emission limitation set by a standard can be achieved in practice by affected sources within the compliance timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA considers deployment timelines, supply chains, workforce, proximity to sequestration, and other practical constraints when concluding achievability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sector or nationwide component of factors in determining the BSER
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether and how EPA considers sector-wide or nationwide considerations (e.g., feasibility across the source category, availability of CO2 transport/sequestration infrastructure) when selecting BSER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA examines inventory of candidate facilities, distance to storage, trunklines, and national infrastructure investments and includes state law/context considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination that CCS is adequately demonstrated for long-term coal-fired steam generating units
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's rationale that carbon capture and sequestration (CCS) is the BSER for long-term coal-fired steam generating units based on simultaneous demonstration of CO2 capture, transport, and sequestration; capture technology demonstrations (e.g., Boundary Dam, Petra Nova); transport demonstrations; and geologic sequestration availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble discusses case studies, EPAct05-assisted projects, vendor and user statements, permitting and rights-of-way, security of CO2 transport and storage, UIC/GHGRP frameworks, timing of permits, and responses to public comments supporting the adequacy finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: CCS capture, transport, and sequestration demonstration subcriteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For CCS to be considered adequately demonstrated EPA examines (A) capture demonstrations at coal-fired units, (B) CO2 transport demonstrations and pipeline examples (including distance considerations), and (C) geologic sequestration site availability and regulatory structure for storage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA looks at industrial CCS examples, CO2 pipeline trunklines, permitting experience, security and monitoring frameworks, EPAct05 projects, and inventories of candidate sequestration sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs specific to CCS (capture, transport, sequestration, and tax credit considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of CCS-specific cost elements: capture costs, CO2 transport and sequestration costs, effect of IRC Section 45Q tax credit, and comparison of total CCS costs to other control costs and prior rulemakings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA presents cost breakdowns and compares CCS costs in historical and present contexts; cost reasonableness is weighed against emission reduction benefits and other factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-air quality and energy impacts specific to CCS
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy penalty and other non-air impacts of CCS (e.g., water use, non-GHG emissions, capture plant siting, transport and sequestration impacts, and impacts on the energy sector).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors are analyzed to determine whether CCS would impose unacceptable non-air harms that would preclude designation as BSER; EPA also considers mitigation and regulatory frameworks (e.g., UIC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for natural gas co-firing as BSER for medium-term coal-fired units
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA rationale that natural gas co-firing is the BSER for medium-term coal-fired units based on adequate demonstration via boiler modifications, natural gas pipeline development, costs, non-air impacts, extent of CO2 reductions, and technology advancement potential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA discusses feasibility of retrofitting boilers, pipeline access, compliance dates, and quantifies expected reductions and costs relative to alternatives such as CCS or heat rate improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options not selected as BSER (partial capture CCS, heat rate improvements, others) and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA documents candidate options considered but not selected as the BSER (e.g., partial capture CCS, natural gas co-firing for some categories, heat rate improvements) and explains legal, technical, cost, or achievability reasons for not selecting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble sections enumerate why particular options were rejected — e.g., insufficient precision, costs, inadequate demonstrated performance, or adverse impacts — providing rationale useful for stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of emission limitation for final standards (long-term and medium-term coal-fired units)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific degree/level of CO2 emission limitation EPA sets for long-term and medium-term coal-fired steam generating units (and the rationale for those levels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA ties degree of limitation to the chosen BSER, evidence of achievable capture or co-firing rates, cost/benefit analysis, and statutory constraints; see sections VII.C.3 and VII.C.3.a–b.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSER determination and multi-part BSER approach for combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: For new and reconstructed stationary combustion turbine EGUs EPA determines BSER components (e.g., lower-emitting fuels, highly efficient generation, hydrogen co-firing, CCS) and can adopt a multi-part BSER and standard of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA evaluates adequacy, costs, non-air impacts, extent of CO2 reductions, and technology promotion for each component and considers phase-based standards (Phase-1, Phase-2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subcategorization criteria for stationary combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria to subcategorize combustion turbines by electric sales/load (low, intermediate, base load), higher heating value basis, thresholds between subcategories, integrated onsite generation and energy storage, definition of system emergency, multi-fuel-fired units, industrial EGUs, and applicability to combined heat and power (CHP) units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble describes legal basis for subcategorization and operational/market thresholds (including changes to base-load thresholds) and special rules for rural/small systems and industrial EGUs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability requirements and fossil fuel-type definitions for steam generating unit subcategories
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on which units are covered (applicability), including coal-fired units permanently ceasing operation before January 1, 2032, sources outside contiguous U.S., IGCC units, and detailed fossil fuel-type definitions for subcategories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA provides definitions, applicability triggers for modified/new/reconstructed units, and special handling for units with planned retirements or unique configurations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of performance structure (Phase‑1 and Phase‑2) for combustion turbines
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment of phased emission standards (Phase-1 standards for base load, intermediate load, etc., and Phase-2 standards) that determine performance levels for new and reconstructed combustion turbines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA specifies different numeric standards and timelines by subcategory/phase and links Phase-1 standard determination to the NSPS review and technological feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing and monitoring requirements — general and CCS-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: General testing and monitoring requirements for affected sources, including specific monitoring and compliance determination procedures for sources implementing CCS (e.g., monitoring capture plant performance, CO2 transport, and sequestration monitoring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes continuous monitoring, QA/QC, monitoring procedures for capture and storage chain, and references to procedures/equations in subparts (e.g., monitoring equations for Subpart TTTT/TTTTa and UUUUb).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping and reporting requirements (notification, reports, and records)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obligations for affected sources to maintain records, submit notifications and periodic reports, and comply with specified reporting formats and timelines under the NSPS and emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions cover general NSPS recordkeeping and reporting, CCS-specific reporting, GHGRP transfer requirements (e.g., requirement that source must transfer CO2 to an entity reporting under GHGRP), and incorporation-by-reference materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance dates and compliance date extension mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified effective and compliance dates (final rule effective July 8, 2024; various compliance dates including January 2032 for some components) and mechanisms by which compliance dates may be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble explains statutory timing, EPA-set compliance dates for subcategories, and administrative criteria/processes for extensions (including interactions with state plan mechanisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan requirements to maintain stringency of EPA's BSER determination
rubrics_metrics.description: States must establish plans that at minimum maintain the stringency of EPA's BSER determinations when setting standards of performance for affected existing EGUs and follow EPA-prescribed approaches for establishing presumptive standards and other requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble and subpart UUUUb detail how states must adopt presumptive standards (or demonstrate equivalent stringency), required plan components, timing, EPA review and action, and potential federal plan triggers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishing presumptive standards and baseline emission performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for establishing baseline emission performance for presumptive standards for fossil fuel-fired steam generating units (long-term coal, medium-term coal, natural gas/oil units), including baseline emission rate definition (CO2 mass emissions and corresponding electricity generation for any continuous 8-quarter period within the 5 years prior to publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may apply presumptive standards using the defined baseline; EPA provides calculation methods and example equations and tables in the subparts and appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remaining Useful Life and Other Factors (RULOF) — thresholds and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Threshold requirements for considering RULOF for less-stringent standards or longer compliance schedules, procedures for invoking RULOF for long- and medium-term coal-fired EGUs, calculation methods to account for RULOF in standards, and contingency requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA provides numerical thresholds, methods for calculating unit-specific adjustments, interaction instructions for using RULOF with compliance date extension mechanisms and reliability considerations, and examples for invoking RULOF to address reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance flexibilities available to states (equivalent stringency; emission averaging/trading; unit-specific mass-based; mass-based trading; interstate trading)
rubrics_metrics.description: A menu of compliance flexibilities states may use if they demonstrate equivalent stringency to EPA's presumptive standards: demonstrating equivalent stringency, rate-based emission averaging, rate-based emission trading, unit-specific mass-based compliance, mass-based emission trading, and interstate emission trading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA lists requirements for demonstrating equivalent stringency, exclusions for certain EGUs from flexibilities, program implementation features, and how interstate trading relates to existing state programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: State plan components, submission timing, EPA action, and federal plan applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Required components of a State Plan submission (general components; specific requirements for these emission guidelines, including meaningful engagement, transparency and compliance assurance), timing of submissions, revision procedures, EPA action on plans, and when/fhow a federal plan may apply or be promulgated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble outlines required documentation, meaningful engagement requirements for affected communities, reporting/transparency expectations, timelines for initial submittal and revisions, and EPA's approvability criteria and federal fallback mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increments of progress and reporting milestones for affected EGUs that plan to permanently cease operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for affected EGUs that plan to permanently cease operations to meet reporting obligations and milestones and to follow increments-of-progress schedules where applicable (particularly for medium-term and long-term coal-fired EGUs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA specifies timelines, milestone reporting elements, and how planned retirements interact with compliance flexibilities and potential RULOF calculations.
